Plant Growth Testing - Intervals from a total of 16 drill holes were subjected to controlled plant growth testing using barley, winter wheat or western wheatgrass. With very few exceptions the intervals tested supported normal plant growth and seed head development, although plant yields were variable. No consistent relationship could be demonstrated between chemical or physical soil characteristics and yield. Six intervals demonstrated atypical or depressed plant growth. Lack of germination in one sample was attributed to a combination of low hydraulic conductivity and overwatering; stunted plants in one sample presumably resulted from high soil acidity. Saline conditions may have accounted for stunted and slightly chlorotic plants in several tests, but a number of samples with similar or higher levels of soluble salts did not adversely affect plant growth. Environmental conditions in the field are decidedly different from those in a greenhouse, but the growth testing data suggest that after topsoiling it is unlikely that plant growth and development will be adversely affected by subsoil traits. Surface Water Hydrology
Drainage Basin Characteristics - Tracts II and III are included in two major watersheds, drained by Tullock and Sarpy Creeks. The main channel of Tullock Creek, which is located several miles west of Tract II, flows generally north to its mouth on the east bank of the Bighorn River near the town of Bighorn, Montana. The total drainage area of Tullock Creek is 446 square miles, of which about 8 square miles, or 1.8 percent, are included in Tract II.
